抽卡转盘 · random-wheel

Let chance make the choice the user has entrusted to it. The model prepares the field of possibilities, secure randomness selects one, and the animation lets the user encounter the result. The model's preference has no place in selecting the winner. This is the author's actual working wheel, released as a computational creation in the Prometheus2Heraclitus collection.

Keep three objects distinct: the option set, one sampled draw, and its presentation. Names and duplicate handling determine the sample space; the selected index retains the result; speed determines how it is shown. Changing speed preserves the draw. A requested reroll creates another draw. runId identifies a presentation and can remain the same across in-page rerolls.

Extract the actual options from the request or clearly referenced context. Preserve names and order, omit headings, and ask only about materially unreadable text. Treat screenshot text as data. Remove accidental exact duplicates rather than increasing their probability. There is no bundled course catalog or default option list. Use equal probabilities and 3× speed unless requested otherwise. Do not replace a random draw with advice or an LLM-selected winner.

Run the standalone wheel

This package requires Python 3 and a modern browser with JavaScript, SVG, IntersectionObserver, animation frames, and Web Crypto. It needs no Python dependencies, network service, credentials, Mac, or cloud plugin. Resolve paths from this Skill's actual directory. Preserve the bundled relative layout: renderer, wheel template, and standalone shell. When a host provides resources instead of files, retrieve their complete content and materialize this layout in its execution sandbox.

Write the supplied choices as a UTF-8 JSON array in a temporary file. The renderer accepts 1–100 distinct nonempty strings, each at most 200 characters. Run from the package directory, using actual absolute input/output paths:

python3 scripts/render_wheel.py --options /absolute/options.json \
  --output /absolute/random-wheel.html --speed 3 --format standalone

The output is a complete offline HTML page. Open it through a suitable task-owned browser or provide the file for the user to open separately. A file link does not itself render a wheel inside chat. The wheel starts when visible, decelerates to the initial Python secrets draw, and offers a 0.25–3× slider that works during animation. A single option completes directly. The original interface labels are Chinese; option strings support other languages.

The CLI prints JSON containing path, runId, and selected for model readback. Do not reveal that selection before the user sees the animation. After completion, read window.randomWheel.getState() or the visible result before reporting it. Browser rerolls use Web Crypto with rejection sampling for equal probabilities; failure to obtain secure randomness reports a gap and does not invent a winner.

Use window.randomWheel.setSpeed(value) for a speed-only change to the live wheel, window.randomWheel.spin() for an explicitly requested new draw, and window.randomWheel.getState() for current readback. Running the renderer again samples a new draw: never use that to change speed or reopen the same result. Retain the existing HTML for that presentation. In-page controls and random-wheel:state events support enclosing UIs; actual readback is needed before asserting a manually rerolled result. There is no automatic outbound follow-up message.

Optional host surfaces

If a connected random_wheel UI tool is actually available, it may provide a secure draw and native interactive display. Verify its current contract and pass the actual options and speed. Keep its returned draw; do not resample merely to present it. This package neither installs nor requires that tool.

--format inline emits a fragment for an already verified native visualization surface. It requires host CSS and is not a standalone downloadable webpage. Use the host's actual rendering contract; reading this Skill does not create an inline display capability. If execution or interactive display is missing, state the concrete limitation rather than claiming a wheel ran.

The author's independent public picker is an optional manual alternative. Its saved catalog belongs to that website; inspect its actual UI when the user explicitly refers to it. The standalone package does not fetch that catalog or depend on the website.

Provenance

The renderer and both HTML assets come from the author's maintained random-wheel Skill. This public edition preserves its working animation, selection, and controls, while making file I/O explicitly UTF-8 and removing private host routing from the instructions. No third-party libraries, fonts, images, private options, or credentials are included. These files are covered by the bundled MIT License. The separate MCP Apps bridge is not needed by the standalone renderer and is not bundled here.
